cards.for: anyone deemed to belong to the Territory

note: The Virgin Islands' card for those who belong to the Territory is the Belonger Card, issued by the Civil Registry and Passport Office (electronic since 2012). Virgin Islands News Online (2012) reported the Registrar-General: the old cards were replaced free for six months from 1 May 2012 and at $30 after that. No current fee for a first card or a replacement, nor the card's term or the time, was found. Tried again 2026-10-30: the Government's site has moved (gov.vg) and its old Civil Registry pages answer 404 with no archived copy; the Department of Immigration's fee structure (December 2025) lists residence and belonger status cards at 10 dollars, 50 under its new fees, but that is the card Immigration issues with a grant of status, not shown to be the Civil Registry's Belonger Card, so the fee stays null.

sources.title: Virgin Islands News Online, Belonger Cards now electronic to curb fraud (2012)
sources.said: In an effort to curb fraudulent duplications of Belonger Cards, the Civil Registry and Passport Office has announced the implementation of electronic cards. ... Members of the public who are deemed to belong to the Territory and are applying for Belonger Cards will now be issued electronic cards as a means to heighten security. ... “Effective May 1, 2012 all persons with the non-electronic Belonger Card will have six months to make an appointment and come in to the office to have the cards replaced free of charge.
